# the contributor audit: cover incidence and the weighted-noise obstruction

## Minimal five-cap circuit overlap: PASS

I read `candidate cad180c3c669dffd`
and ran its exact verifier. The bounded rational complementary simplex,
all five strict mixed deletion witnesses, all ten possible triples,
all ten two-group failures and the positive-area source witnesses pass.

The actual barycentric coordinate map has full rank. Its projected
pentagon stays inside the displayed lattice-free square. Each projected
group condition is the weighted sum of the ORIGINAL cap margins. The
five positive continuous circuits exhaust the rank-two possibilities;
there are no hidden positive pairs. The private-cap counting argument
correctly includes every possible number of selected groups. Small
squares at the strict mixed witnesses realize essential caps on an
actual full-dimensional source, including all additional hull fibers.
The example makes no low-budget or extremal-depth assertion.

## High-cardinality defect budget and nine-cap boundary: PASS

I read `candidate f8a85d598f5eddb1`
and ran its verifier: all 27 circuit tests, all nine strict mixed
witnesses, four uniquely forced groups, 2300 incidence checks and exact
actual-source masses pass.

The defect identity counts unused group slots, rank deficits and repeated
cap occurrences exactly. Inclusion-minimality is used at the right point
to ensure that every original cap occurs in the selected group union.
The private-cap lower bound and the bound on groups meeting any shared
cap follow by ordinary union counting; they do not infer a stress or
a compatible geometric variation from incidence alone.

The nine-cap example's four group inequalities force integer base sum1
and first coordinate strictly between0 and1, proving mixed freeness.
They also bound the base, and one positive circuit bounds the continuous
fiber, so the complementary polyhedron is bounded. The strict real
feasible point and strict mixed deletion witnesses make all nine original
facets essential. Exactly one copy of each of the three continuous
directions forms a positive minimal circuit. The four indicated base
points force the three disjoint rows and the fourth cross-circuit.

The actual source has the four binary vertex fibers exactly as given.
All cap areas, including the four full square contributions, agree with
the displayed rational numbers. Its maximum depth is certified by
finite isolation tilts and the ordinary triangle maximum, and remains
above OC. In n=d=2, a hypothetical strict below-M/9 cover needs at least
ten original caps, precisely where the positive private-cap count
applies IF the required original-cap circuit selection is available.
That availability is not assumed for every bounded-source cover.

## Weighted-tail preservation under symmetric noise: PASS

I read `candidate 347c99fa827e699e`
and ran its standard-library verifier. The six tails, every-positive-
coefficient formula, strict proper perturbation, continuous-noise margin,
and 515 exact lattice fibers pass.

The base triangle tail is exactly 1-4q^2 on its proper interval. The
six-tail deficit is lambda/9 for every positive coefficient, with no
supporting-boundary atom. The epsilon perturbation makes every variable
component cut proper and the fixed full/empty ones strict; its exact
rational deficit checks. The globally4-Lipschitz tail controls the
independent continuous-noise smoothing with the stated remaining margin.

I independently proposed and checked the actual lattice-product extension.
The base polytope has exact sections[(q-1)/2,(q+1)/2]^(n-1), hence endpoint
multiplicities2^(n-1) and exactly one central integer point. The resulting
weighted-tail gap is (1-m lambda)/[9(2m+1)], negative for sufficiently
large n for EVERY fixed lambda>0. In n=2, lambda=7/9 gives exactly-1/81.
Its scalar normal is genuinely oblique in the original ambient space,
and its center has integer base and lies in the actual source.

The product's exact maximum depth4/9 is independently certified: reflected
base pairs use the already proved ordinary paired-tail theorem for the
lower bound, and the three cylindrical canonical triangle caps give the
matching upper bound at every candidate. Vertical closed caps retain
the central fiber and at least one member of each pair. Thus this is
an auxiliary preservation counterexample with a full OC-safety proof.
